purpose: Retain implementation and source counterexamples; no erased frozen outputs
resolved_development_failures: Passing a multiline string to the Astropy CDS reader with a separate ReadMe caused it to interpret the text as a filename. Retried using immutable decoded files with the exact catalog table names.
The local Astropy ascii.read wrapper supplied fill defaults incompatible with CDS blank numeric fields. The independent ascii.Cds reader correctly preserves the catalog null masks.

An initial parser rejected missing trailing columns and the P4 PGC052336 name-only row. The final parser accepts omitted null tails only for hash-verified released rows; independent CDS parsing matches every checked field.
An initial comparison treated a blank Astropy string flag differently from null. Both readers now retain this source absence as null.

An initial test asserted an unjustified absolute 0.01 agreement with the published stellar coefficient. The final test uses the already-declared config relative tolerance 0.001. The actual 0.0343195 percent difference is explicitly retained; no experiment gate was changed.
retained_scientific_limitations: Published stellar coefficient and the coefficient independently computed from printed input constants differ slightly.
The recovered 2009 HERACLES HTML R21 scaling direction conflicts with the stated line-ratio definition; only independently checked algebra and fixed reference normalization are used.
Catalog means/SDs and P4 flags do not constitute independently measured 3D geometry.
Seventeen FITS headers carry inherited MJy/sr labels for colors, masks or coverage; semantics require the publisher documentation.
access_note: Required full catalog and publication bytes include incidental systemic-velocity or spectral-header fields. The recovery never reads a rotation-curve dataset, motion residual or field array and uses no such values for fitting or scoring. Source FITS payloads were hashed as bytes; only headers were interpreted.
sings_pdf_review: The web screenshot endpoint failed to recognize the PDF content type. The exact downloaded PDF was rendered locally with PyMuPDF and pages 5 and 8 visually inspected. Private PNGs were not published.
